title: OTWD moderation decision
description: The recorded outcome of a moderation decision, with who or what decided and why. Most decisions decide a submission. A moderator can also decide, without a submission, to revert earlier changes or to take content down (ADR 0036). Decisions are appended to the submission log and never edited. An appeal produces a new decision that refers to the earlier one. Decisions are not published: partner apps see the summary in a submission's status, and moderators read them through the moderation endpoints.

subject.description: What the decision is about. submission: a submission, named in submission_id, with how routing sent it. revert: undoing earlier changes, listed in revert. takedown: removing content, described in takedown. Open: a reader treats a subject it does not know as an action it cannot show in detail.

submission_id.description: For subject submission: the submission decided.

outcome.description: The outcome. For edited_and_approved, amendments lists the corrections.

routing.description: How routing sent the submission to whoever decided it, with what routing read from the submission: its kind, its record type and the fields it touches. The fixed checks derive whether the submission is on the always-human list from these, using the creation kinds, closures, merges and the safety fact markers (x-otwd-safety-fact) in the record type's schema, so a routing rule cannot approve one by declaring always_human false.

route.description: human_review: a moderator's queue. auto_approval: approved by a routing rule, never used for the always-human list (new records of every record type, closures, merges, safety facts).

submission_kind.description: The kind of the submission decided.

record_type.description: The record type the submission creates or changes.

fields.description: For update_facts and confirm_facts: every fact and facility the submission sets, removes or confirms.

always_human.description: True when the submission is on the always-human list. The fixed checks derive it, and it must be true whenever the kind or a field puts the submission on the list.

fixed_check_flags.description: Fixed-check results that send a submission outside the always-human list to a person all the same. Like always_human, the fixed checks set them and routing only reads them. accessibility_raised: the submission raises wheelchair access for any feature of a site or ferry service to yes, sets step_free_access or changing_places to true, or sets toilets.key_required to false. A wrong yes there can strand a traveller, while a wrong no costs far less, so only the raise goes to a person.

verdict_ids.description: The verdicts available when the decision was made. A verdict informs a decision and is never one.

code.description: For example confirmed_by_seed_source, duplicate_of_existing_site or copied_text.

public_note.description: The message shown to the contributor and returned to the partner app. Required for rejected and needs_info.

amendments.description: For edited_and_approved: each amendment the moderator made before approving, with the submitted and the applied value.

applied.description: The value as applied, or null when the moderator dropped the field.

merge.description: For an approved request_merge: the surviving record and the records that now redirect to it, all of one record type.

change_seqs.description: For approved and edited_and_approved: the changes the decision produced. A merge produces one change per record involved.

appeal_of.description: When this decision answers an appeal: the decision appealed against.

revert.description: For subject revert: the changes undone, and why. Each produces a change with origin revert.

cause.description: appeal_upheld: an appeal showed the change was wrong. abused_api_key: the changes came through an API key that was compromised or abused (ADR 0039). vandalism: deliberate false or harmful edits. moderator_error: a moderator approved something by mistake. Open: a reader treats a cause it does not know as moderator_error.

api_key_id.description: For abused_api_key: the key whose changes are reverted.

takedown.description: For subject takedown: what was removed and why. Who asked for it is never recorded here or published. A takedown request is handled as a restricted case under the moderation policy, outside the submission log.

reason.description: The same reasons as a change's takedown_reason.

retract_record.description: True when the whole record is retracted, leaving only its stub.

unmerge.description: For an approved request_unmerge: the restored record and the record it had been merged into.

split.description: For an approved request_split: the record split and the new records made from it, all of one record type.

replacement.description: For an approved request_replacement: the replaced record and the new record of another type that replaces it.

allOf.description: A decision on a submission names it and says how routing sent it. A revert or takedown is a moderator's own action, with no submission and no routing, and it applies at once.

A routing rule may only approve, only on the auto_approval route, and only a submission outside the always-human list that no fixed check flagged for a person. The fixed checks derive membership of the list from routing's submission_kind, record_type and fields, so the always_human false required here is a cross-check, never the rule itself.

Decider.description: Who or what made the decision. moderator: a person. routing_rule: an automatic approval rule in the fixed routing code, allowed only outside the always-human list. The AI never decides.

moderator_id.description: Moderators are contributors with moderation rights, so they use contributor IDs.
